subject: Immediate: Request to priority-pin Helio traffic + exec bridge for 5xx/latency spike
messages:
From: Jamie Park <jamie@heliohealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: sre-ops@heliohealth.com
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 09:12:34 -0800
Subject: Latency + 5xx spike affecting billing pipeline (urgent)

Hi Sean —

We started seeing an increase in 5xx responses and end-to-end latency from Redwood starting ~08:40 PST. This is impacting our end-of-day billing job (batch calls to embeddings + rerank) — failures are causing retries and ballooning costs.

What we see:~30% 5xx on /v1/batch/generate, median p99 latency jumped from 220ms to 1.8s, retry loop is saturating downstream queues. Attached is a small sample of error traces and dashboard screenshot.

Can Redwood route our traffic to a different region or apply a temporary priority for our calls? We need a mitigation path within the hour — this is blocking our billing close.

—Jamie
Senior SRE, Helio Health
[attachment: helio_error_samples.log (text/log)]
[attachment: latency-dashboard.png (image/png)]

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 09:18:05 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Latency + 5xx spike affecting billing pipeline (urgent)

Forwarding Helio escalation — they report rising 5xx and p99 latencies impacting a time-sensitive job. They asked if we can either: 1) reroute their traffic to a different region, or 2) apply a temporary "priority-pin" to reduce their error surface while we investigate.

Immediate asks:
- Hannah: can we spin a constrained cross-region reroute (pin to us-west-2) + emergency KV cache warming for Helio?
- Dev: if we need to enable a temporary throttling/fail-open policy or a per-tenant prioritization flag, what's the fastest safe path?
- Marissa: we may need to brief execs for a small temporary credit if this hits billing — please prep numbers.

I'll open an ops bridge in 5 mins unless you advise otherwise.

Thx,
Sean
Account Exec (Escalations)
Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 09:22:47 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency + 5xx spike affecting billing pipeline (urgent)

On Tue, Feb 28, 2028 at 09:18, sean_gallagher@redwood.com wrote:
> Forwarding Helio escalation — they report rising 5xx and p99 latencies impacting a time-sensitive job.

Acknowledged — we're seeing correlated tail latency on the telemetry side (backend queue depth rising and increased kernel-level NVMe latency on the us-east-1 pool). Initial triage:

Plan (T-0 + 30m):
- Open ops bridge: INC-20280228-47 (I've started the bridge).
- Short-term mitigation: apply a tenant-level priority-pin that pins Helio's routing to us-west-2 cold-warm pool, enable prefix KV cache for their keyspace, and reduce batch concurrency from 8->4 for their tenant. This reduces chances of KV misses and improves cold-start amplification.
- If priority-pin not possible in config, do a live traffic split at the edge: 80% -> us-west-2, 20% -> us-east-1 until healthy.
- Engineering action: Dev, can you deploy the prioritization flag as a hotfix (config toggle) and open a safe rollback? We need this in <20m.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Cost: routing to us-west-2 (higher spot pricing at peak) + reduced batching will increase per-token cost during mitigation.
- Statefulness: requests that rely on local cache may have a higher miss rate until prefix warming completes.

I'll post telemetry links to the bridge.

-Hannah
Sr. Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed-traffic-split.md (text/markdown)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 12:03:21 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency + 5xx spike affecting billing pipeline (urgent)

Thanks team —

Saw the bridge notes and Hannah's mitigations. From an account/exec angle: Helio runs a high-value billing workload (contract MRR tier + committed capacity). I'm recommending we:

- Approve the priority-pin + 80/20 live split now. Estimated incremental cost: ~$1.9k/hr while active (projected for 3 hours worst case).
- Offer Helio a one-time credit of ~10% on the impacted day's usage to offset retries as a customer-satisfaction gesture (we can finalize exact amount after postmortem).
- Ask Helio to share any additional request IDs for failed jobs so we can match logs for the post-incident RCA.

Dev — Hannah needs the toggle live ASAP. If we get the toggle, I'll authorize the cost and call the bridge for an exec sync (10 min) to confirm approvals.

Sean — please communicate the plan to Helio (I drafted a short note below).

--- draft for Helio — please edit before send ---
Jamie,

We opened an ops bridge and are implementing a short-term mitigation: pinning your traffic to our us-west-2 pool and applying an 80/20 live split while we stabilize. We expect reduced 5xx and improved tail latency within ~30 minutes of the toggle. We will cover any incremental cost for mitigation and propose a one-time credit to offset retries.

Working on a detailed RCA and will share as soon as we have root cause.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
